FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Met on the sourced no-fee limb for the route's own instrument: no participant filing arises in the ordinary case, so no filing fee does, and the delivered guidance page says so under 'WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHETHER A WAIVER EXISTS'. Two held sources agree: the controlling decision ('the participant ordinarily files nothing') and the compiled New York profile (src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/NY-new-york.json, fee table line 'Automatic sealing (160.50/160.55/Clean Slate) $0 No filing'). For the two ancillary costs the workflow itself creates, the packet states that no committed record it binds prices the certificate of disposition or the criminal-history result and names the clerk of the sentencing court and the New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services as the offices that answer. Observation, not a failure: the compiled NY profile prices the certificate of disposition ($5 per case outside NYC, $10 in the five boroughs) on lines keyed 'Required for each 160.59 case' and records 'DCJS record review (your own record) DCJS fee' without an amount; under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A3 a line keyed to the § 160.59 petition does not establish this § 160.55 route's figure, and the packet's sentence about the records it binds is literally accurate. Whether the certificate fee is route-independent is an owner call this verifier does not make; it would be a one-sentence instruction change if it is.

SERVICE.detail: Met on the affirmative nobody-is-served limb with the mechanism that replaces it. The decision records 'The clerk notifies DCJS and appropriate law-enforcement agencies'; the delivered guidance page states under 'WHO MUST BE SERVED, AND WHO IS NOTIFIED': 'Nothing is served, because in the ordinary case nothing is filed. The committed decision records that the CLERK notifies DCJS and the appropriate law-enforcement agencies. The request page in this packet is a letter to the sentencing court, not a pleading served on an opposing party.' participant-instructions.md adds that sending the certified disposition to DCJS is a transmission, not service. The compiled NY profile holds no service rule for § 160.55 ('no form — sealing is directed by the court / done by OCA-DCJS').

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The decision holds three stops: 'motion or counsel if court previously entered an interests-of-justice nonsealing order', 'A pre-November 1, 1991 qualifying case may require a motion under the statute's legacy branch', and CONTESTED NONSEALING: ATTORNEY HANDOFF. The delivered page 'WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP INSTEAD' carries all three, plus DWAI (CPL § 160.57(1)(a)), needing the court file closed (which § 160.55 does not do) and any immigration question; 'WHERE TO GO WHEN SELF-HELP STOPS' names DCJS for the record and a motion or counsel for the rest; numbered step 6 in participant-instructions.md says 'stop' on a prior nonsealing order. 'WHAT YOU DO NOT DO' bars filing a sealing petition first and conflating Clean Slate. The signing line and date are refused and the packet states it is not legal advice, not sent for you and seals nothing by itself. 3/3 held stops carried.
